subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded internal cache for provider-normalized tool schema parameters now, and what invalidation boundary should it use?
rationale: The source-level repeated work is clear, but the permanent boundary affects provider hooks, plugin metadata lifecycle, custom provider behavior, and the prepared-runtime migration direction.

options.title: Refresh the bounded cache
options.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR so known bundled normalizers can cache cloned schema parameters while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared runtime
options.body: Keep the issue open until the broader prepared-runtime rollout carries enough provider/tool facts to avoid a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Hold implementation until current-main Google/Gemini live proof or heap evidence confirms the user-visible impact still occurs.

recommendation.title: Refresh the bounded cache
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR so known bundled normalizers can cache cloned schema parameters while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: The cache lifecycle decision intersects the prepared-runtime migration tracker and provider-runtime boundary that mcaxtr authored.
